clue.text: Strip back mature herb

indicators.note: going back means the word for strip is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: to strip someone of goods is to rob them
to mature is to age

explanation.surface: A cook peels back a seasoned herb before using it.
explanation.definitionFit: Borage is a blue-flowered plant whose leaves are used in salads and drinks, a classic garden herb.

clue.text: Religion's founder had to change, following upward call

indicators.note: in a down clue, going upward means the word for call is read bottom to top
letters made to change are rearranged into a new order

blocks.note: to dub someone is to call or name them
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A religion's founder had to change his ways after hearing a calling from on high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' is the order word: the rearranged letters come after the upturned call, and dub is an old verb for naming someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Siddhartha Gautama, known as the Buddha, established Buddhism in ancient India.

clue.text: Rebels getting right sign about development

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the right sign wraps round the development

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right
gradual development, as of species
a sign of the zodiac, the ram

explanation.surface: Insurgents receive a favourable omen about how events will unfold.
explanation.walkthrough: Right and the sign together make one wrapper, and the development slots in between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolutionaries are people who rise up against an established government or order, as rebels do.

clue.text: Hide rage, tooth being broken

indicators.note: something broken has its parts scattered, so these letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone conceals their fury after losing a tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: To go to earth is a hunting phrase: a fox goes to earth when it bolts into its burrow.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to go into hiding, from a hunted fox disappearing into its den.

clue.text: Bird after time swallowed by snake in country

indicators.note: whatever is swallowed ends up inside the swallower, here the snake

blocks.note: a boa is a large constricting snake
T is the abbreviation for time
a swan is a large water bird

explanation.surface: In some land, a bird is eaten by a snake once enough time has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After time' puts the bird after T, and that pair goes inside BOA.
explanation.definitionFit: Botswana is a landlocked nation in southern Africa, bordering South Africa and Namibia.

clue.text: Unknown book possessed by sailor? Correct

indicators.note: something possessed is held within its owner, so the book sits inside the sailor

blocks.note: OS stands for ordinary seaman
B is the abbreviation for book
to cure a fault is to correct it

explanation.surface: A sailor owning an unfamiliar book is asked to confirm it.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure describes someone or something little known and not famous, hence unknown.

clue.text: Stick with workforce

blocks.note: first meaning: a long walking pole or rod
second meaning: the employees of an organisation

explanation.surface: Someone sticks with the people they employ.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a wooden rod carried in the hand and the body of people working for an employer.

clue.text: Mad scene, amateur getting excited in area with gaming machines

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up and agitated, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A novice gets carried away in a crazy scene at the slot machines.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement arcade is a hall full of coin-operated games and fruit machines, often at the seaside.

clue.text: A requirement, almost, to keep chapter with point in story

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the requirement is dropped
to keep something is to hold it inside, so the shortened word surrounds what follows

blocks.note: taken as written
a need is a requirement
C is the abbreviation for chapter
a dot is a small point

explanation.surface: Telling a tale needs chapters and punctuation in the right places.
explanation.walkthrough: The shortened requirement keeps its final letter outside, so chapter and point sit between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short amusing or interesting tale about a real incident or person.

clue.text: Part of boot that's excellent, up among best

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for excellent is read bottom to top
among means placed in the midst of, so the word for best surrounds it

blocks.note: the top is the best
ace means excellent in informal speech

explanation.surface: Someone praises a boot as top-notch.
explanation.definitionFit: A toecap is the reinforced covering over the front of a shoe or boot, protecting the toes.

clue.text: Studies including verse, part of Bible I love, and prayers

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the word for studies wraps round everything listed after it

blocks.note: a den is a private study room
V is the abbreviation for verse
OT is the Old Testament
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A devout reader's study sessions take in Bible verses they love, alongside prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Devotions are acts of religious worship, especially private prayers said regularly.

clue.text: Perceptive account, subtle except for odd parts

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters leaves only the second, fourth and so on

blocks.note: AC is the abbreviation for account
the even letters of this word are kept

explanation.surface: An insightful report is nuanced apart from a few odd passages.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute mind is sharp and quick to notice things, just as a perceptive one is.

clue.text: Narrator of novel could handle life differently

indicators.note: doing something differently means rearranging it, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A troubled storyteller wishes he could have coped with life another way.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits the character neatly: the teenage narrator struggles to cope with adult life.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the teenage first-person storyteller of J D Salinger's The Catcher in the Rye.

clue.text: Leading renegades in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means moving backwards, so the word for renegades is read from the end

blocks.note: a rat is a deserter or traitor

explanation.surface: The ringleaders of a band of deserters fall back.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, star means principal or most prominent, as in the star player leading a team.

clue.text: Common foil containing aluminium

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the word for foil wraps round the metal

blocks.note: to foil a plan is to prevent it
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Ordinary kitchen foil is made of aluminium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foil' looks like the kitchen wrapping but works as a verb meaning thwart.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prevalent is widespread and found generally, so it is common.

clue.text: Completely consumed, filled with endless bad temper

indicators.note: endless means without an end, so the last letter of the word for bad goes
being filled with something means holding it inside, so the shortened word sits in the middle

blocks.note: all means completely, as in all alone
evil means wicked or bad
consumed food means ate it

explanation.surface: Someone is utterly eaten up with a nasty mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad temper' reads as one phrase, but 'bad' belongs to the wordplay and 'temper' alone is the definition, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to moderate or soften it, which is what alleviating pain or hardship does.

clue.text: Power held by faction with unusual range

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it, so the faction wraps round power

blocks.note: a sect is a breakaway group or faction
P is the symbol for power in physics
rum is an old-fashioned British word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A political faction holds power and has an unusually broad reach.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a full range of related qualities or ideas, such as the political spectrum.

clue.text: Visionary man with muscular movement after support

indicators.note: after places the man and his twitch behind the support, so the support comes first

blocks.note: a prop is a support
he is the pronoun for a man
a tic is an involuntary twitch of a muscle

explanation.surface: A seer twitches involuntarily once he has something to lean on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After support' puts PROP first, with the man and the twitch following it.
explanation.definitionFit: Prophetic means foreseeing the future accurately, which is what a visionary person does.

clue.text: Lights necessary to assist orchestra

indicators.note: what is necessary to a phrase forms an essential part of it, so look inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and into the second

explanation.surface: Musicians playing in the dark need lights to help them see.
explanation.definitionFit: Torches are portable lamps, called flashlights in American English, so they are lights.

clue.text: Container inadequate without right cover

indicators.note: without right means the abbreviation for right is taken away from the word for inadequate

blocks.note: a can is a tin container
ropy is British slang for poor in quality

explanation.surface: A poorly made box lacks a proper lid.
explanation.walkthrough: Ropy is everyday British slang for shoddy or below par; drop its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy is an overhead covering of fabric or another material, sheltering what lies beneath.

clue.text: Delayed dish, quietly taken away

indicators.note: something taken away is removed, so the abbreviation for quietly is dropped

blocks.note: a plate is a dish
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A waiter discreetly clears away a meal that arrived too late.
explanation.definitionFit: Late means arriving after the expected time, so delayed in a dictionary sense.

clue.text: Sensitive bid

blocks.note: first meaning: sore or painful to the touch
second meaning: a formal offer to supply goods or do work at a price

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a delicate offer; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for tenderness or soreness and also a noun for a formal offer made in a competitive process.

clue.text: Man stared, never prepared to give exact reference

indicators.note: something prepared is made ready by being worked over, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: chap is informal British for a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man gazed but was never ready to cite his source precisely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like part of the fodder, but it gives CHAP and only the next two words are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from citing scripture precisely, and now means the exact source or full detail of anything.

clue.text: Catch up with tips from older singer

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for catch is read bottom to top
the tips of a word are its two ends, so only its outermost letters are kept

blocks.note: to net a fish is to catch it
the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: Someone catches up with a veteran singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with the highest natural adult male voice in a choir.

clue.text: Give up disregarding small rule

indicators.note: disregarding something means leaving it out, so the abbreviation for small is dropped

blocks.note: to resign is to give up a post
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A minor regulation is ignored and someone gives up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small rule' reads as a phrase, but 'small' belongs to the wordplay and 'rule' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule as a monarch, holding sovereign power over a realm.

clue.text: Random expression of disgust brought about by risk

indicators.note: brought about is the nautical sense of turning round, so the expression faces the other way

blocks.note: pah is an exclamation of contempt
a hazard is a risk or danger

explanation.surface: A random snort of disgust is provoked by danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought about by' looks like 'caused by', but 'brought about' turns PAH round and 'by' simply joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Something haphazard lacks any plan or order, so it happens at random.

clue.text: Lack of confidence in film with evidence of corrosion

blocks.note: a mist is a thin film, as of condensation on glass
rust is the visible sign that iron is corroding

explanation.surface: A movie about corrosion fails to inspire belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' suggests a movie, but here it is a thin layer like condensation.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistrust is a feeling of suspicion or doubt about someone, the absence of trust or confidence.

clue.text: Appearance made by last pair of children in turn

indicators.note: the last pair means only the final two letters of the word are taken
in means placed inside, so the selected letters go within the word for turn

blocks.note: to veer is to turn sharply
the final two letters of this word

explanation.surface: The youngest two children each take their turn to appear.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a superficial outward show that hides the reality beneath, a mere surface appearance.
